He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Denver Pioneers men's basketball|Denver Pioneers]].{{cite web|title=Ade Murkey - University of Denver Athletics|url=https://denverpioneers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/ade-murkey/2779|work=DenverPioneers.com|access-date=April 19, 2021}} ==High school career== Murkey attended [[St. Croix Lutheran Academy|St. Croix Lutheran]] where he led the Crusaders to a 29–3 record as a senior, averaging 22 points, 9.9 rebounds, 4.2 assists and 2.0 steals per game and setting the single season scoring record, while also becoming the school's all-time leader in assists and steals. For this, he was named to the Minnesota AP Boys' Basketball Third Team All-State. ==College career== Murkey played [[college basketball]] for [[Denver Pioneers men's basketball|Denver]], seeing action in 118 career games, starting 88, while averaging 10.6 points, 4.0 rebounds and 2.0 assists per game.{{cite web|title=TIMBERWOLVES SIGN ADE MURKEY|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-sign-ade-murkey|work=NBA.com|date=December 3, 2020|access-date=April 19, 2021}} As a senior, he averaged 18.6 points and 6.3 rebounds per game and was named to the 2020 All-[[Summit League]] Second Team. His best game came on February 14, 2020, when he scored a Denver Division I program record 42 points against [[South Dakota State Jackrabbits men's basketball|South Dakota State]].{{cite web|title=Ex-St. Croix Lutheran star Ade Murkey chasing NBA dream|url=https://kstp.com/minnesota-sports/denver-ade-murkey-nba-draft-prospect-timberwolves-clippers/5811933/|website=KSTP.com|date=July 2021|url-status=dead}} ==Professional career== ===Iowa Wolves (2021)=== After going undrafted in the [[2020 NBA draft]], Murkey signed on December 3, 2020, an [[Exhibit 10]] deal with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Stinar|title=Ade Murkey Realizes NBA Dream With Hometown Minnesota Timberwolves|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/benstinar/2020/12/13/timberwolves-rookie-ade-murkey-playing-for-hometown-team/|work=[[Forbes]]|date=December 13, 2020|access-date=March 26, 2022}} and was waived on December 19, after one preseason appearance.{{cite web|first=Mark|last=Suleymanov|title=Timberwolves Sign Zylan Cheatham, Waive Ade Murkey|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2020/12/timberwolves-sign-zylan-cheatham-waive-ade-murkey.html|work=HoopsRumors.com|date=December 19, 2020|access-date=April 19, 2021}} On January 25, 2021, he signed as an affiliate player with the [[Iowa Wolves]] of the [[NBA G League]],{{cite web|first=Randi|last=Burrell|title=Wolves Announce 2021 Roster|url=https://iowa.gleague.nba.com/news/wolves-announce-2021-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=January 25, 2021|access-date=April 19, 2021}} where he played 13 games and averaged 7.1 points, 2.3 rebounds and 0.9 assists in 21.7 minutes per game.{{cite web|title=Ade Murkey Player Profile|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Ade-Murkey/Summary/107672|website=RealGM.com|access-date=April 19, 2021}} ===Stockton / Sacramento Kings (2021–2022)=== On October 13, 2021, Murkey signed with the [[Sacramento Kings]],{{cite web|first=Leo|last=Tochterman|title=Kings sign Ade Murkey and Damien Jefferson to contracts|url=https://www.sactownroyalty.com/2021/10/13/22724657/sacramento-kings-sign-ade-murkey-damien-jefferson-contracts-g-league|website=SactownRoyalty.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=October 13, 2021|access-date=October 18, 2021}} but was waived three days later.{{cite news|first=Jason|last=Anderson|title=Kings waive summer league standout Emanuel Terry; finalize roster for regular season|url=https://www.sacbee.com/sports/nba/sacramento-kings/article255048272.html|work=[[The Sacramento Bee]]|date=October 16, 2021|access-date=October 18, 2021}} He subsequently joined the [[Stockton Kings]] on November 2.{{cite web|title=Stockton Kings Announce 2021-22 Training Camp Roster|url=https://stockton.gleague.nba.com/news/stockton-kings-announce-2021-22-training-camp-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 25, 2021|access-date=November 2, 2021}} In 12 games, he averaged 11.8 points, 3.0 rebounds and 1.7 steals per game.{{cite web|title=Kings Sign Ade Murkey|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-ade-murkey|website=NBA.com|date=December 22, 2021|access-date=December 22, 2021}} On December 22, 2021, Murkey signed a 10-day contract with the [[Sacramento Kings]]. He made his debut the same day against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]], accumulating no points, rebounds or assists in one minute of action.{{cite web|title=Ade Murkey 2021-22 Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/m/murkead01/gamelog/2022|website=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=March 26, 2022}}{{cite magazine|first=Ben|last=Pickman|title=In It for a Minute|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2022/02/22/nba-one-minute-club-daily-cover|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=February 22, 2022|access-date=March 26, 2022}} On January 1, 2022, Murkey was reacquired and activated by the [[Stockton Kings]] after the 10-day contract expired.{{cite web|title=2021-2022 Stockton Kings Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Stockton-Kings/56/Transaction_History/2022/|website=RealGM.com|access-date=January 2, 2025}} Murkey joined the Sacramento Kings for the [[2022 NBA Summer League]]. On October 24, 2022, he re-signed with the Stockton Kings,{{cite web|title=2021-2022 Stockton Kings Transaction History|url=https://stockton.gleague.nba.com/news/stockton-kings-announce-2022-23-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2022|access-date=January 2, 2025}} however, he did not make the final roster. ===Wisconsin Herd (2024–2025)=== On October 28, 2024, Murkey joined the [[Wisconsin Herd]].{{cite web|title=WISCONSIN HERD ANNOUNCES 2024-25 TRAINING CAMP ROSTER|url=https://wisconsin.gleague.nba.com/news/wisconsin-herd-announces-2024-25-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=October 29, 2024}} ===Álftanes=== In September 2025, Murkey joined Álftanes.{{cite news |author1=Ingvi Þór Sæmundsson |title=Annar fyrrverandi leikmaður Sacramento Kings til Álftaness |url=https://www.visir.is/g/20252774292d/annar-fyrrverandi-leikmadur-sacramento-kings-til-alftaness |access-date=12 September 2025 |work=[[Vísir.is]] |date=12 September 2025 |language=Icelandic}}
